given: LEGACY BEHAVIOUR ONLY - this specification documents what the PyQt6 app does, for migration/characterisation tests. It is NOT the target behaviour; see "answer". Given: the app is in single-view mode (main_window.view_mode == "single"); cat.png is the current image (main_window.current_image_path); the in-memory segment list is empty (segment_manager.segments == []); beside the image on disk sit cat.npz, cat.txt and cat_coco.json (and none of cat_CM.npz, cat_seg.txt, cat.xml, cat_createml.json); the selected export formats are the defaults {NPZ, YOLO_DETECTION}; "Auto-Save on Navigate" is ON (its default); there are no pending polygon points and no pending AI segment preview (Enter commits either of those first, and a committed one would add a segment and take the image off this path).
when: Any save is triggered for that image. In this configuration there are five distinct triggers, all of which converge on save_export_manager.save_single_view_output (save_export_manager.py:97-133): (1) the user presses Return or Enter (hotkey "save_output"/"save_output_alt", config/hotkeys.py:67-69 -> main_window.py:1014 -> keyboard_event_manager.handle_enter_press:187-234, which reaches main_window._save_output_to_npz:1993-1998 at line 205, 230 or 234); (2) the user picks another file in the file tree, with auto_save on (file_navigation_manager.py:157-160); (3) the user navigates next/previous, with auto_save on (file_navigation_manager.py:271-274); (4) in sequence view, the timeline moves to a different frame, with auto_save on (main_window.py:3424-3427 -> _auto_save_sequence_frame:3480-3519, which temporarily points current_image_path at the frame being left, line 3494-3496); (5) "Save All Propagated" in sequence view, which is NOT gated by auto_save (main_window.py:4741-4825, saving at 4813). In every case the check at save_export_manager.py:107 - `if not self.segment_manager.segments:` - is evaluated before the export-format setting is read at 118-120, and on an empty list control goes to _delete_associated_files (line 108) and returns at 109 without writing anything.
then: _delete_associated_files(cat.png) (save_export_manager.py:523-542) calls delete_all_outputs (core/exporters/__init__.py:209-215), which walks EXPORTERS.values() in registration order - coco, createml, npz, npz_class_map, pascal_voc, yolo_detection, yolo_segmentation (import order, core/exporters/__init__.py:224-230) - and for each exporter calls delete_output(image_path), which computes os.path.splitext(image_path)[0] + <that format's suffix>, and if os.path.exists() then os.remove()s it (identical five-line body in all seven: coco.py:102-107, createml.py:69-74, npz.py:32-37, npz_class_map.py:49-54, pascal_voc.py:65-70, yolo_detection.py:48-53, yolo_segmentation.py:58-63). Seven paths are probed - cat_coco.json, cat_createml.json, cat.npz, cat_CM.npz, cat.xml, cat.txt, cat_seg.txt - and the three that exist are permanently removed: cat_coco.json, cat.npz, cat.txt. cat_coco.json is deleted even though COCO JSON was never a selected format: the selected-format set is not consulted on this path at all. The file-tree row for cat.png is refreshed (save_export_manager.py:531-534) and a neutral notification is shown whose text is exactly "Deleted: cat_coco.json, cat.npz, cat.txt" - the deleted paths in the iteration order above, basename only, joined by ", " (save_export_manager.py:536-538) - followed by _update_all_lists() and QApplication.processEvents() (539-540). No confirmation dialog is shown before or after (there is no QMessageBox anywhere in save_export_manager.py or main_window.py) and there is no undo entry. CONTRAST, same image with 2 segments: the empty check at 107 is false, export_all (core/exporters/__init__.py:189-206) runs only the two selected exporters and never deletes, so cat.npz and cat.txt are overwritten, cat_coco.json is left untouched on disk, and the notification reads "Saved: cat.npz, cat.txt" (save_export_manager.py:124-126).
and: And the deletion is unconditional on provenance, content and history: delete_output tests only os.path.exists on a name derived from the image's basename. Nothing records who wrote the file, whether LazyLabel ever read it, whether the user changed anything this session, or whether the image loaded successfully - there is no dirty flag and no "user cleared the annotations" flag anywhere on the path. And the only guard before the delete is `if not self.mw.current_image_path` (save_export_manager.py:102-104, warning "No image loaded."); if nothing was found to delete the user instead gets the warning "No segments to save." (save_export_manager.py:541-542). And in multi-view the same destruction runs through a different function with different rules: main_window._save_multi_view_annotations (6559-6636) loops `for viewer_idx in range(2)` (6581) and calls delete_all_outputs directly at 6590 when that viewer's segment manager is empty; it never reads auto_save, and its three navigation callers (main_window.py:6497 _load_next_multi_batch, 6530 _load_previous_multi_batch, file_navigation_manager.py:402-403 load_multi_view_from_path) do not check auto_save either, so turning Auto-Save off does not stop deletion in multi-view. And multi-view deletion is silent - a logger.debug at 6592 only (no "Deleted:" notification, no "No segments to save."), while pressing Enter in multi-view still reports success: "Multi-view annotations saved!" (save_export_manager.py:592-593) even when the call only deleted files. And the deletion is not transactional: delete_output has no try/except, and in single view the call at 106-109 sits outside the try that starts at 111, so if os.remove raises (a file locked by another process on Windows) the loop stops part-way with some files already gone, and the exception escapes save_output -> _save_output_to_npz into file_navigation_manager.py:160/274, which has no handler, aborting the navigation; the sequence path (main_window.py:3498-3517) and the multi-view path (6588, 6635-6636) catch and log it instead.
parameters: Deleted path formula: os.path.splitext(image_path)[0] + suffix, probed and deleted in this exact order (EXPORTERS dict insertion order, set by the import block at core/exporters/__init__.py:224-230): 1. "_coco.json" (coco.py:100), 2. "_createml.json" (createml.py:67), 3. ".npz" (npz.py:30), 4. "_CM.npz" (npz_class_map.py:47), 5. ".xml" (pascal_voc.py:63), 6. ".txt" (yolo_detection.py:46), 7. "_seg.txt" (yolo_segmentation.py:56). Exactly seven ExportFormat members exist (core/exporters/__init__.py:14-23). The order matters only if a test asserts the notification string. The class-aliases file <base>.json is NOT in this set and is never deleted on any live path (see edge cases). Trigger predicate: `not segment_manager.segments` evaluated at save time (save_export_manager.py:107) - no other condition. Selected export formats are irrelevant to deletion (read only at 118-120, after the early return at 109). Defaults: export_formats = {NPZ, YOLO_DETECTION} (config/settings.py:8-9, mirrored at core/exporters/__init__.py:60-63); at least one format must stay selected - unchecking the last one re-checks it (ui/widgets/export_format_widget.py:94-103); auto_save = True (config/settings.py:45, ui/widgets/settings_widget.py:43 and 200), labelled "Auto-Save on Navigate" (settings_widget.py:39). Exact user-visible strings: "Deleted: " + ", ".join(basenames) (save_export_manager.py:536-538, neutral notification); "No segments to save." (542, warning); "No image loaded." (103, warning); "Saved: " + ", ".join(basenames) on the write path (125); "Multi-view annotations saved!" (593, success); "No AI segment preview to accept" (ui/managers/ai_segment_manager.py:127-128). Multi-view processes only viewer indices 0 and 1 (main_window.py:6581), regardless of the 2_view/4_view grid setting.
edgeCases: Nothing exists to delete: delete_all_outputs returns [], so no file-tree refresh and no "Deleted:" notice - the user sees the warning "No segments to save." instead (save_export_manager.py:529, 541-542).
No image open: save_single_view_output returns at 102-104 with the warning "No image loaded."; nothing is written or deleted.

Enter in any mode other than polygon first calls _accept_ai_segment (keyboard_event_manager.py:231-233). With no preview pending the user sees "No AI segment preview to accept" (ai_segment_manager.py:127-128) and line 234 still runs the save, so the deletion happens anyway. With a preview pending, accepting it adds a segment and the save writes files instead.

Enter in single-view polygon mode first finalises pending polygon points (keyboard_event_manager.py:198-202); polygon_drawing_manager.finalize_polygon returns immediately if fewer than 3 points (172-173), so 1-2 stray points do not save the image from deletion, but 3+ do.

Enter in sequence view while in polygon mode does nothing at all: handle_enter_press branches only on view_mode "single" (198) and "multi" (206) inside the polygon branch, with no else, so no save and no deletion occur (keyboard_event_manager.py:193-230).

Multi-view navigation deletes with Auto-Save OFF: _save_multi_view_annotations (main_window.py:6559-6636) never reads auto_save and is called unconditionally by _load_next_multi_batch (6496-6497), _load_previous_multi_batch (6529-6530) and load_multi_view_from_path (file_navigation_manager.py:402-403).

Multi-view deletion is invisible: only logger.debug (main_window.py:6591-6593). Enter in multi-view then reports "Multi-view annotations saved!" (save_export_manager.py:592-593) even when the operation only deleted files.

The eighth file <base>.json (class aliases) is NEVER deleted by any reachable path. _delete_multi_view_files (save_export_manager.py:544-567) does delete it, but its only caller is _save_viewer_output (454-521, call at 519), and _save_viewer_output has zero callers in src/ or tests/. Both are dead code; a rewrite must not reproduce them.

"Save All Propagated" in sequence view is not gated by auto_save (main_window.py:4741-4825). It clears the segment manager per frame (4776) and skips any propagated mask that is not 2-D after squeezing (4781-4784); if every mask for a frame is skipped the list stays empty, all seven sidecars for that frame are deleted at 4813, and the frame is still marked saved at 4814 with a green timeline status at 4815-4818.

Deletion is by filename only, with no provenance or content check, so any same-named file is destroyed: a caption file cat.txt written by another tool is deleted as if it were YOLO Detection output, and cat.xml metadata as if it were Pascal VOC (yolo_detection.py:48-53, pascal_voc.py:65-70).

Sibling-image collision: the suffixes are not reserved namespaces. Saving an empty foo.png deletes foo_seg.txt and foo_CM.npz, which are the YOLO-Segmentation and NPZ outputs of the different images foo_seg.png and foo_CM.png. Likewise foo.png and foo.jpg in one folder share every sidecar name, so emptying one wipes the other's annotations.

A sidecar that loads successfully but yields zero segments stops the load chain and dooms the healthy files behind it: load_existing_mask returns at file_manager.py:205 after the first format that does not raise, so an NPZ with neither "mask" nor "masks" (silent return at 241-242), a _CM.npz with no class_map or a shape mismatch against the image (298-300, 309-311, 313-318), or a .txt whose lines do not have exactly 5 fields (433-434, plus the ValueError skip at 437-440) all leave 0 segments with no error - and the next save deletes every sidecar, including the lower-priority .xml or _coco.json that was never even read. Load-chain order is .npz, _seg.txt, _coco.json, _CM.npz, .xml, _createml.json, .txt (file_manager.py:128-136).

CORRECTED from the card: a sidecar that RAISES while loading does NOT by itself cause this. file_manager.py:202-204 logs the exception and `continue`s to the next format, so a corrupt top-priority file still lets a healthy lower-priority one load. Only the silent-zero-segment returns above (and an unreadable image, next item) produce the empty list.

An image that cannot be decoded still gets its sidecars deleted. In load_image_by_path the order is: current_image_path = path (file_navigation_manager.py:276), _reset_state() (279, which clears the segment manager at main_window.py:2140-2141), segment_manager.clear() (281), then cv2.imread returns None and the function returns at 299-302 with no annotations loaded. The undecodable image is now the current image with an empty list, so the next auto-save navigation deletes all seven of its sidecars.

The sibling path load_selected_image returns even earlier, at file_navigation_manager.py:175-176, when QImage cannot read the file - after current_image_path was reassigned at 162 but before _reset_state() at 186 - so the PREVIOUS image's segments stay in memory attached to the new path; the next save writes them under the new image's basename, or, if that list was empty, deletes the new image's sidecars.

Partial deletion on I/O error: delete_output has no try/except, so a locked file raises mid-loop and the remaining formats are never probed. In single view the delete runs outside the try block (save_export_manager.py:106-109 vs the try at 111), so the error propagates out through file_navigation_manager.py:160/274 and the next image never loads; sequence mode (main_window.py:3498-3517) and multi-view (6588, 6635-6636) swallow it into the log.

Write-path asymmetry worth pinning in the same test: with segments present, a SELECTED format can still be skipped, leaving a stale file of that very format on disk - npz.py:15-17 returns None when the mask tensor is empty, yolo_detection.py:19-22 and 35-36 and yolo_segmentation.py:28, 46 return None when no annotations are produced, npz_class_map.py:22-26 when nothing is active, coco.py:85 and createml.py:51 likewise. export_all only reports paths actually written (core/exporters/__init__.py:198-206).

An active crop is applied to the written masks (save_export_manager.py:412-417, crop_coords from crop_manager.current_crop_coords) but has no effect on the deletion path, which never builds an ExportContext.

Documentation contradicts the code and must not be used as the contract: core/exporters/__init__.py:192-196 states that writing never deletes and that neighbouring files "may be ... ground truth that shipped with the dataset", and ARCHITECTURE.md:193 says delete_all_outputs is "Used only when the image has no segments left, i.e. the user cleared the annotations". The code makes no such check. The comments at main_window.py:3499 and 3515 also claim only the NPZ is deleted; all seven formats are.
answer: DECISION (already made by the product owner, recorded here so no implementer re-opens it): the rewrite uses explicit save with dirty tracking and NEVER deletes an annotation file without an explicit user action, so this legacy behaviour is a defect to be fixed, not reproduced - deletion must not be inferred from an empty in-memory segment list, must not extend to formats the user did not select, and must not touch files LazyLabel did not write in the current session. Everything in given/when/then/and/parameters/edgeCases above is therefore a description of LEGACY behaviour, intended only for characterisation tests that pin the PyQt6 app before/during migration and for a deliberate, documented divergence note; it is not a target specification, and a TypeScript implementer must not treat it as one. What the card got wrong: (1) the notification order was implied as "cat.npz, cat.txt, cat_coco.json" but delete_all_outputs iterates EXPORTERS.values() in import order (core/exporters/__init__.py:212 with the import block at 224-230), so the real string is "Deleted: cat_coco.json, cat.npz, cat.txt" (save_export_manager.py:536-538); (2) the Given omitted the preconditions that actually gate the path - single-view mode, auto_save on, and no pending polygon points or AI preview, both of which Enter commits first (keyboard_event_manager.py:198-202, 231-234; polygon_drawing_manager.py:172-173); (3) the When named only two of five triggers - it missed sequence-frame change (main_window.py:3424-3427 -> 3480-3519), Save All Propagated (main_window.py:4741-4825, ungated by auto_save, deleting a frame's files at 4813 when every mask fails the 2-D check at 4781-4784 while still marking it saved at 4814), and the whole multi-view family (main_window.py:6497, 6530; file_navigation_manager.py:402-403 -> main_window.py:6589-6594), which deletes even with Auto-Save OFF, silently, while Enter still reports "Multi-view annotations saved!" (save_export_manager.py:592-593); (4) the edge case claiming that annotations which "failed to load" leave 0 segments is wrong as stated - file_manager.py:202-204 catches a raising loader and continues down the chain, so a corrupt file does not hide a healthy one; the real hazard is a loader that returns silently with nothing (file_manager.py:241-242, 298-300, 309-311, 313-318, 433-440) and thereby ends the chain at file_manager.py:205; (5) the card's "and" was null and its parameters string was a triple-concatenated duplicate of the suffix list with three near-identical edge cases repeated (the "No image loaded" case appeared twice and the unrelated-.txt case three times) - all deduplicated; (6) I REFUTE the first compliance judge's "eighth file" finding: <base>.json is deleted only by _delete_multi_view_files (save_export_manager.py:544-567), whose sole caller _save_viewer_output (454-521, call at 519) has no callers anywhere in src/ or tests/, so it is dead code and the live multi-view path (main_window.py:6590) deletes the same seven files as single view. What an implementer must watch for if they ever run this legacy path for comparison: deletion is name-derived only (splitext(image)[0] + suffix, no provenance check), so it collides with sibling images (foo.png wipes foo_seg.txt and foo_CM.npz, the outputs of foo_seg.png and foo_CM.png) and with same-stem different-extension pairs (foo.png / foo.jpg); it is non-transactional (no try/except in any delete_output, e.g. npz.py:32-37, and in single view it runs outside the try at save_export_manager.py:106-111, so a locked file leaves a half-deleted set and aborts navigation); and it fires on an image that never decoded, because file_navigation_manager.py:276-281 sets current_image_path and clears the segment manager before cv2.imread fails at 299-302. Finally, the executable code - not the prose - is the rule: core/exporters/__init__.py:192-196 and ARCHITECTURE.md:193 both assert guarantees the code does not implement, and main_window.py:3499/3515 claim only the NPZ is removed when all seven formats are.
corrections: Given: added the missing preconditions - single-view mode, Auto-Save on Navigate ON (default), no pending polygon points, no pending AI preview - and stated explicitly that the card documents legacy behaviour, not target behaviour.

When: expanded from 2 triggers to the 5 that reach save_single_view_output (Enter, file-tree selection, next/previous navigation, sequence frame change, Save All Propagated) with the auto_save gate identified per trigger, plus the separate multi-view family that bypasses auto_save entirely.

Then: fixed the deletion/notification ORDER to registration order - the notice is exactly "Deleted: cat_coco.json, cat.npz, cat.txt", not the card's implied order; added that all seven candidate paths are probed and the four absent ones skipped, that no confirmation and no undo exist, and kept the 2-segment contrast case.

And: filled in the previously null field with the no-provenance/no-dirty-flag clause, the multi-view divergence (ignores auto_save, silent, false success message, only viewers 0 and 1), and the non-transactional partial-deletion behaviour with its differing error handling per path.

Parameters: rewrote the garbled triple-concatenation into one statement; kept the seven suffixes (re-verified char-for-char) but put them in real iteration order with per-file citations, added the exact user-visible strings, the auto_save default, and the fact that the selected-format set is read only after the early return.
Edge cases: deduplicated (the 'No image loaded' case appeared twice, the unrelated-.txt/.xml case three times) and reduced the crop case to its true scope (write path only, no effect on deletion).

Edge cases: CORRECTED the failed-load case - a raising loader is caught and the chain continues (file_manager.py:202-204); only a silently-empty loader stops the chain at 205 and dooms the healthy lower-priority files.
Edge cases: added multi-view deletes with Auto-Save OFF; multi-view deletes silently while Enter reports success; multi-view only touches viewers 0 and 1 (main_window.py:6581).
Edge cases: added Save All Propagated as an ungated trigger that deletes a frame's files and still marks the frame saved (main_window.py:4781-4784, 4813-4818).
Edge cases: added Enter in sequence view + polygon mode does nothing at all (keyboard_event_manager.py:193-230 has no sequence branch).

Edge cases: added the undecodable-image paths - load_image_by_path clears segments before cv2.imread fails (file_navigation_manager.py:276-302), and load_selected_image returns before _reset_state so the previous image's segments end up attached to the new path (162 vs 175-176 vs 186).
Edge cases: added non-transactional partial deletion and its divergent error handling (save_export_manager.py:106-111 vs main_window.py:3498-3517 vs 6588/6635).

Edge cases: added the write-path asymmetry - a SELECTED format can be skipped when it produces no annotations, leaving a stale file of that format (npz.py:15-17, yolo_detection.py:19-22/35-36, coco.py:85, createml.py:51, npz_class_map.py:22-26, yolo_segmentation.py:28/46).

Edge cases: REFUTED the judge's 'eighth file' finding - <base>.json is deleted only from dead code (_delete_multi_view_files at save_export_manager.py:544-567, reachable only from _save_viewer_output at 454-521, which has no callers); recorded as must-not-reproduce.
Edge cases: added the doc/code contradictions as an explicit do-not-trust note (core/exporters/__init__.py:192-196, ARCHITECTURE.md:193, main_window.py:3499 and 3515).
Answer: recorded the settled decision that the rewrite never deletes without explicit user action, so this rule is captured as a legacy defect for migration tests rather than as target behaviour.
